name: Hackian
operator: Ethiack (the vendor); each customer is the operator of its own use
basis: Ethiack's own public pages (product, documentation, blog, customer stories, legal and security pages)
what: AI agent that runs reconnaissance, exploits vulnerabilities with non-destructive routines and reports findings with proof of exploitation; used in Continuous Adversarial Exposure Validation and in Agentic Pentests (Swift, Depth).
note: A scan of a product as its vendor documents it, not of any one deployment. Made by the report studio: a researcher-assessor, a challenger, then the scorer. Part of the first Portuguese cohort.
grant_note: Not measured. No deployment shape for this product is published in the capability grammar.

findings.finding: Level 4 Autonomy rests on this answer (with I08 and I10). I19 reads: full autonomy within boundaries; the person monitors. The cited policy page supports the first half: it says 'an agentic test relies on this policy to make decisions in real time' and that Guardrails define what the agent must not do. It says nothing about a person monitoring. The note adds 'findings and the activity log show its progress', which comes from the agentic-pentests page (findings appear as discovered) and the test-details page (Activity log), not from the cited source. The CTO post says the vendor team reviews traces after execution, which is the vendor, not the customer. The agentic-pentests page also says scope, policy and credentials cannot be edited once an Agentic Pentest is launched, and no page read gives a pause or stop control for an Agentic Pentest (the pause control is documented for continuous tests only). The evidence is an artefact (documentation of a policy editor and an activity log), not an adjective, but the answer should cite the page that shows the monitoring half or say it is drawn from two pages. The level survives because I18 is not claimed; the word 'monitors' is only partly sourced.

Source (CAEV page) does say Hackian 'continuously analyzes your entire attack surface in breadth', with wildcard assets and reconnaissance, so it works across many assets and domains of one customer. Grade documented and mode default are right. But I10 is the second leg of Autonomy 4 and the only leg of Reach 2 in effect (I11 is available only with a Beacon). Breadth over one customer's assets is a weak reading of 'runs multi-step workflows across systems or coordinates other agents'. A stronger artefact is on the policy-guidelines page: 'Hackian uses Primary Focus to distribute work across multiple agents'. It is not credited; consider citing it. For Reach 2 (Integrated: documented connectors to common tools) no connector or integrations page was cited; the level rests on surface breadth and the Beacon, not on connectors.

Beacon page opens with 'The Ethiack Beacon securely extends the Ethiack Hackian Engine testing capabilities into your internal networks.' The span is in the source, under fifteen words. Mode available is right: the customer must install the Beacon and expose CIDRs. Crossing a trust boundary into customer networks via an outbound tunnel is shown. Credited correctly.

Span is in the CTO post, but it sits in a general section 'Building a Hackbot: The Four Core Components', describing tools an agent can have ('giving the hackbot a virtual machine or API access'), not stated of Hackian's shipped product. The indicator is generating and executing code with privileges. The post speaks of executing commands or sending requests, not code generation; the product page lists 'Non-destructive exploit generation' and may be a better source. No level uses I04 (Autonomy is carried by I08 and I19), so no level changes; the note should say the post describes the architecture in general.

Test-details page says Activity is 'A log of the actions Hackian has been performing during the test'. Span present. The indicator needs operation: it counts only when observed or measured. It is graded documented, so it is correctly not counted; Control stays at level 1 and I41 appears in no level. Pause (I39) is documented for continuous tests only. Mode default is fine.

Test-details page: 'For Continuous Adversarial Exposure Validation tests, the header also includes a control to pause or restart the test'. Span is a fragment present in the source and under fifteen words. It pauses a continuous test, not individual agent actions, and applies to continuous tests only. Fine for a documented answer; it does not feed a level.

Span 'Hackian, our agentic AI pentester, runs against U.Porto's exposure 24/7' is in the case study, and it names a customer, so the In production badge is supported. Figures are asset counts (1,000 critical assets within 5,000), not sessions or tasks, but a named customer is sufficient. The note also says 'Jumia and CEGID case studies also name Hackian'. I searched every fetched Ethiack source of the scan (including the case study and product page) and neither name appears. Remove that clause or add and cite the source for it.

The documentation llms.txt resolves (HTTP 200) and contains '- [Overview](/docs/api): Ethiack REST API documentation.' as well as portal and test pages. Grade observed by probe is right. Note it also feeds Openness 3 only with I50, but Openness is capped at level 1 here. Note: the span is the REST API description line; the note says it indexes portal, API and test documentation, which is true of the file. Not an interface for agents to call (S4 not claimed): correct.

Benchmark post says 'our own agent Hackian led on both F1 and recall under the same protocol' (13 words, present). Results are published, including Claude Code and PentAGI comparisons, and the protocol is described as published on arXiv and adaptable. The results are the vendor's own run of the vendor's own benchmark, and the post states Hackian is not in the paper itself. The note says 'open EthiBench protocol'; 'published' is what the page shows, 'open' is a stretch. Does not change a level (Openness 3 is not reached).

Findings-details page says 'Edit severity and score: adjust the severity or CVSS score assigned to the finding'. Present and under fifteen words. That is a customer's own edit control, not a channel to report problems or contest output to the vendor. The Updates feed is described as 'A chronological feed of status changes and comments between all participants', with 'ethical hackers or triagers', where participants are those of an engagement (written there for Expert engagements). The page also has 'Ask Hackian'. Cite the Updates sentence and say it is shown for engagements with triagers, or lower the grade of the claim to what is shown. No level changes (Openness stays 1).

Product page: 'It autonomously executes benign exploitation routines to confirm vulnerabilities.' Exact, 9 words. Documented, default, credited to the right indicator (the product itself executes the action). It is a vendor marketing page, so documented is the correct ceiling.

Agentic Pentests page: 'Hackian performs a focused, in-depth analysis of a defined set of assets'. Present, under fifteen words. It states purpose and the Swift and Depth variants. Right grade and mode.

Span is in the Expert Pentests page: 'technologies and test types that Hackian does not currently handle on its own, such as mobile applications'. It names a scope limit, not known failure cases. The CAEV page also says it covers common vulnerabilities, 'prioritizing coverage over depth'. The benchmark post discusses error rates of agents. Together O1 (Disclosed: I20 plus I22) holds on a scope limit; consider saying in the note that this is a scope limit, which is what the evidence is.

Policy-guidelines page: 'Guardrails define what the agent must not do.' present, with four standard guardrails written by the customer in prose. Right indicator, documented, default. It carries Control 1. It is a customer-written instruction, not an enforced limit; Control does not claim more.

Card computed: A4, R2, C1, O1 (sum 8). Level 4 Autonomy rests on I08, I19 and I10: all three are vendor documentation, not observed operation, and the I19 monitoring leg and the I10 'orchestrate' reading are the soft points (see those findings). Reach 2 rests on I10 plus an available-only Beacon (I11). Control and Openness are 1 each; Balanced would not apply (A minus one is 3). The announced-features list (MCP server, execution visibility) is correctly not credited. I did not verify the scan's announced sources or the lowered answers I05, I25, I36, I48, I54, I56, I58. Assessment and not_credited record lowered items; not_credited is empty.

Round one: partly answered. The studio swapped the source to the continuous-validation page and the claim now rests on it alone. The span 'Hackian will immediately begin testing the assets in scope, continuously' is present, but it shows a scheduled always-on mode, not an agent deciding anything. The earlier source, the policy-guidelines page, had the decision-making wording ('relies on this policy to make decisions in real time'); this page says only that Hackian 'runs broad checks for common vulnerabilities' and 'prioritizing coverage over depth'. The monitoring half is 'findings ... appear in the Findings section in real time' and 'an alert is raised immediately so your team can act': that is a person acting on results afterwards, which is the closer reading of I18/I19 only if the person watches the run. No sentence says the customer monitors the agent. The note is accurate to the page; the weakness is that the answer now evidences continuous operation more than autonomy with a monitoring person. This answer carries the whole of Autonomy 3 and 4: Autonomy 3 needs I08 plus any of I17, I18, I19, and only I19 is credited. Remove I19 and Autonomy falls to 0 (no I15, I16 or I07 credited), which would void the card under the rule that no card sits below level one in every dimension. Suggest citing the policy-guidelines span as well, or saying in the note that the page shows continuous autonomous testing and alerts, not a person watching the run.

Round one: partly answered. Studio kept it and recorded the Primary Focus 'multiple agents' sentence as not credited under the I12 scope; I verified that sentence is on the policy page and that the not-credited reason is right. The span 'Hackian continuously analyzes your entire attack surface in breadth' is exact and the page also says it monitors 'your domains and surface'. It shows breadth over one customer's assets (wildcard assets, recon), which is a thin reading of 'several domains or systems', and is the second leg of Autonomy 4 ('across systems or coordinates other agents'). Grade documented and mode default are right. Reach 2 does not depend on it alone: I11 (Beacon, available) also satisfies any(I10, I11).

Round one: partly answered. The new source (Support Portal page) is real and the span 'Add a step by step guide of how you reproduce the issue.' is exact (12 words); the note matches the page's ticket guidance. But the page is the general Ethiack support page: it does not name Hackian, the agent or its findings, and describes tickets 'with Ethiack' about 'the unexpected outcome you are seeing'. The note says 'problems with the platform', which is honest, yet the indicator is a channel to report problems with the agent or contest its output. Either say in the note that the page covers the Ethiack platform and does not name Hackian, or find a page that ties the channel to findings or Hackian. This is the only answer Openness 3 would use (with I50); Openness stays at 1 because Openness 3 needs I50 and any of I57, I54, S3, and the cumulative ladder stops at 1 only if level 2 is missing: level 2 needs two of I22, I58, I61 and only I22 is credited, so O1 holds, but a reader should know the I57 credit is general-platform.

Changed span not in the round-one diff, re-read. The span 'tests, the header also includes a control to' is present on the Test Details page (8 words) but stops before 'pause or restart', so the span alone does not show the claim; the next words on the page are 'pause or restart the test depending on its current status'. The note (continuous tests only) is right. No level uses I39 (Control 3 needs I41, I39 and I43; I41 is operation-scoped and I43 is not claimed).

Studio response true: the note now says scope limit. Span 'technologies and test types that Hackian does not currently handle on its own' is on the Expert Pentests page (cited as human-in-the-loop); the note matches the sentence. Openness 1 depends on I20 plus I22 alone (I56 and I58 not credited): remove I22 and Openness is 0. The evidence is a routing statement for human-led tests, not a documented failure case. The continuous-validation page's 'prioritizing coverage over depth' is a closer statement of a limit and could be added.

Studio response true: the Jumia and CEGID clause is gone and the note now says only what the U.Porto page says. The span 'Hackian, our agentic AI pentester, runs against U.Porto's exposure 24/7' is exact, 10 words, and the page says 'entire external attack surface'. The studio's response quotes a CEGID sentence from a page that is not a source of this scan; that is in the review record only, not in an answer or note, so no fix is needed. Customer is named for the capability that acts, so In production holds.

Card computed: A4, R2, C1, O1 (sum 8, Building). Arguing against Autonomy 4 (Orchestrates, 'runs multi-step workflows across systems or coordinates other agents; a person sets goals and reviews outcomes'): it rests on I08, I10 and I19, all vendor documentation graded documented, mode default, nothing observed. I08 is a product-page sentence ('autonomously executes benign exploitation routines'): marketing wording, an artefact only in the sense that it is a stated claim. I10 is breadth over one customer's attack surface, not workflows across systems or coordinating agents; the page that does speak of multiple agents is correctly not credited. I19 is the single point of failure (see its finding): remove it and Autonomy is 0 and the card cannot be published; remove I10 and Autonomy is 3, Reach still 2 through I11. Mode is honest: only I11 is marked available. Autonomy 4 is therefore a literal pass of the rule on thin evidence, and the label 'Orchestrates' reads stronger than the pages. Argue against Reach 2 (Integrated, 'documented connectors to common tools'): neither credited answer is a connector; the Integrations page (Slack, Jira Cloud, Splunk, webhooks, CI/CD) is correctly not credited to I11 as it is platform routing, so the level name overstates what the rule found, though the rule is met. Control 1 and Openness 1 are single-source (I47; I20 plus I22) and honest. Balanced does not apply. Not re-checked: the lowered answers and the announced sources.

Verified answered or unchanged and correct against freshly fetched pages: I04 removed and recorded in not_credited with a reason that matches the product page and CTO post; I50 note now says published on arXiv, Ethiack's own run, and the post does say 'Hackian isn't in the paper itself'; the span is 13 words in the page; I11 Beacon page has the span and 'the beacon initiates the tunnel automatically', mode available with cfg beacon is right; I08, I20, I47 spans exact, under fifteen words, right indicator; S3 llms.txt resolves (200) and contains the REST API description; I41 is documented and correctly not counted (needs operation). Note on style: none of the changed notes contain em-dashes, addresses or at-signs. Round-one findings fully answered: 12 of 15; partly answered: I19, I10, I57.

I08.n: Hackian runs exploitation routines itself to confirm vulnerabilities.
I08.span: It autonomously executes benign exploitation routines to confirm vulnerabilities.

I10.n: In continuous mode Hackian works across the whole in-scope attack surface, not one system.
I10.span: Hackian continuously analyzes your entire attack surface in breadth

I11.n: With a Beacon deployed by the customer, Hackian reaches into the customer's internal networks over a tunnel.
I11.span: securely extends the Ethiack Hackian Engine testing capabilities into your internal networks

I19.n: The test page shows the customer's policy, which cannot be edited once a pentest has started, and an activity log of the actions Hackian performs that gives the customer visibility of the test's progress.
I19.span: giving clients visibility into what is being tested and how the assessment is progressing

I20.n: The documentation states what an Agentic Pentest by Hackian is for.
I20.span: Hackian performs a focused, in-depth analysis of a defined set of assets

I22.n: The documentation states a scope limit: test types Hackian does not handle on its own, such as mobile applications, go to human testers.
I22.span: technologies and test types that Hackian does not currently handle on its own

I39.n: A continuous test page has a control to pause or restart the test; the page gives it for continuous tests only.
I39.span: the header also includes a control to pause or restart the test

I41.n: Each test page carries an activity log of the actions Hackian performs.
I41.span: A log of the actions Hackian has been performing during the test

I47.n: The customer writes guardrails in the test policy, in prose, stating what the agent must not do.
I47.span: Guardrails define what the agent must not do.

I50.n: Ethiack publishes its own run of Hackian against other agents under EthiBench, a protocol published on arXiv; the post says Hackian is not in the paper itself.
I50.span: our own agent Hackian led on both F1 and recall under the same protocol

I57.n: Customers open tickets about the Ethiack platform in its Support Portal, with steps to reproduce and the unexpected outcome; the page does not name Hackian or its findings.
I57.span: Add a step by step guide of how you reproduce the issue.

S1.n: A named customer, Universidade do Porto, runs Hackian continuously against its external exposure.
S1.span: Hackian, our agentic AI pentester, runs against U.Porto's exposure 24/7

S3.n: The documentation site publishes an llms.txt that resolves and indexes the portal, API and test documentation.

not_credited.what: I04 (generates and executes code with privileges)
not_credited.why: The CTO post describes the tools of a hackbot in general (executing commands, sending requests, a virtual machine), not of Hackian as shipped; the product page's 'exploit generation' and 'builds and executes sophisticated exploit chains' do not show code executed with local or cloud privileges. No level used it.

The policy page says 'Hackian uses Primary Focus to distribute work across multiple agents'; it does not show agents with their own context and authority passing work between them, which the indicator's scope requires.

not_credited.what: I11 through the Integrations page (Slack, Jira Cloud, Splunk, webhooks, CI/CD)
not_credited.why: These are integrations of the Ethiack platform that route findings and alerts into the customer's tools, not tools the agent uses across a trust boundary.

not_credited.what: I57 through the finding Updates feed
not_credited.why: The feed of comments 'between all participants' is described with ethical hackers and triagers of an engagement; the Support Portal is the general channel and is cited instead.

not_credited.what: I57 through the Invalid finding status
not_credited.why: The status flow page defines Invalid as 'usually assigned to vulnerabilities that are false positives' but does not say the customer can set it or contest a finding with it; it is a status, not a channel.

Neither credited Reach answer is a connector the agent uses; the Integrations page (Slack, Jira Cloud, Splunk, webhooks, CI/CD) routes the platform's findings and stays not credited to I11. The level is met by the rule any(I10, I11), not by connectors.
